metadata.title: SpaceX takes unconventional route to pricing its stock ahead of IPO

content.text:
It's SpaceX IPO Eve (SPAX.PVT) and Elon Musk's space company is setting its IPO price on Thursday night, taking an alternate route to offer stock at $135 per share rather than a general range.
Yahoo Finance Senior Reporter Pras Subramanian breaks down this unconventional public stock offering.
SpaceX is expected to go public on the Nasdaq this Friday, June 12, under the ticker SPCX.
One of the most anticipated IPOs is nearly here with SpaceX. It's final stretch of gearing up to go public and taking a different route when it comes to pricing. Yahoo Finance's Pras Subramanian joins us here with a closer look. We just got some news, Pras.
Bring us up to speed. What do we need to know?
Yeah. Well, pricing right before the bell. Uh SpaceX has confirmed that 135 that price that they had that they had listed in their prospectus will be the IPO price. That's that's they confirmed it today in a filing or just about half hour ago.
Uh, you know, this is an unconventional process.
Explain that. Explain that a bit.
You know, typically what happens is that the firm that wants to go public, they'll they'll put out a range, a pricing range. Uh, they'll market the stock to different institutions, uh brokerages, etc. Got to kind of get an idea of demand, how much supply they got to fill. And depending on that, they'll maybe go higher in the range or lower in the range depending on what how things are going.
SpaceX was like, no, this is it. It's 135. Uh, you know, people seem to think that's Musk's, Musk is, this is what the price is going to be. This is the fair price for it. Uh, you know, it's whether it's fair or not, that's another story in terms of valuation, but that's what they all, they marketed at. Uh, and that's what it's going to be. So it's a confirmed that it will be the IPO price of 135. And then tomorrow, uh, the stock will have a debut. We'll see what happens on that first pop.
Well, I want to ask you, okay. So it starts starts trading tomorrow. What should we be watching? What are you going to be watching?
You know, we're going to see, you know, Nasdaq last really huge thing that was was was was Facebook, Facebook, right? Several years ago. Didn't go too well. We now are being told that it's going to be a much smoother process. You know it's a lot of stock, $75 billion worth of stock, right? Uh, 555 million shares or there about, something like that are going to be going out there, right?
Uh, so it's a big placement, but supposedly things will be okay. So we'll we'll wait for that first trade. And you know, you talk to some people out on the street and it's they're saying, you know, the perfect move is a 20% pop. That means that the stock was priced properly. You get a nice little bump for people that own the shares, everyone's happy, right? Too, if it's much higher than that, you priced it incorrectly. God forbid it goes lower, right?
So, uh, that's where we're, that's where we're looking at what's going to be that initial pop? Where does it close? And then how does it, how does it then trade for the next few weeks?
Uh, you point out in your story here, IPO shares running four times over oversubscribed. What do you make of that?
Well, it's interesting, right? Because then on its face seems bullish, right? Four times amount of stock is being requested for what's out there, right? But you know how these things work, right? The banks will will the brokerages and banks will will will will basically put in a larger offer than what they actually need to make sure they get an allocation, right? So that if they have 100 million shares that they need to fill, give me 200 million.
Just to make sure they get some, they get half of it at least, right? So there's that. There's also the the talk that, you know, we're talking about Cerberus, right? That was a 20 times oversubscribed stock, right? Um, now it's a much smaller float, but that's a that was they're saying four times is not that great.
It's not that great. You you probably want even more than that. So there's some give and take, there's some differences of opinion as to what that means. On the face of it, it seems like, hey, there's there's there's a lot of interest there. We're seeing numbers like $100 billion in retail uh desire for the stock. We're seeing uh Blackrocks of the world, $10 billion orders, things like that.
So, we're hearing a lot of bullish things, but are they just being floated out? It's coming coming too easy. Every hour we're getting a headline from Reuters, from Bloomberg, from whoever, people are floating out different numbers. This is going well, this is going great. More more interest, more demand. So, it all it all matters when it actually starts trading. That's when we know what happens.
